title: PR posture & lightweight refactor notebook — sidra
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad collecting heuristics and tiny experiments for making PR review less noisy and safer. Not a policy doc — more like a habit-and-tooling checklist I can iterate on.

High-level goals:
- Reduce cognitive overhead per PR (so reviewers can land faster).
- Lower blast radius for refactors (small, reversible steps).
- Give authors clear signals about what reviewers need to focus on.

Notes to self / assumptions:
- Most reviewers have ~20–30 minutes for a pass. Make diffs digestible in that time.
- Tests + simple examples are the strongest accelerators.
- Danger areas: routing/runtime logic, kv-cache edge cases, schema migrations, auth boundary changes.

PR Posture checklist (author):
- TL;DR at top of PR: 1–2 sentences describing change + one-sentence rollback plan.
- Scope bullet: what is intentionally out-of-scope.
- Key files changed: short list for quick scan.
- Runbook snippet if failure mode impacts runtime: what to do, how to revert.
- Tests included? unit/test matrix, and which CI jobs are expected to run. If flaky, call it out.
- Perf surface: any expected latency/regression (local/benchmark numbers).
- Migration notes (schema/contract changes): compatibility guarantees.
- Feature flag / rollout plan: how will this be deployed and rolled back?

Quick reviewer heuristics (my mental model):
- Safety first: find changes that affect dataflow (auth, routing, persistence), verify invariants.
- Behavioral delta: what will change for users? Are defaults preserved?
- Simplicity check: could author have split this into 1) mechanical rename/refactor and 2) behavior change? If yes, request split.
- Test quality: do tests actually assert invariants or just exercise happy path? Prefer explicit assertions.
- Observability: will failure produce a clear error and trace? If not, flag.

Refactor prioritization matrix (tiny mental model):
- Quick wins (<=30 min review + small test): internal renames, dead code removal, small helper extraction. Ship fast.
- Medium (1–3 reviewers, still <2 days): logical reorg, local API consolidation, non-breaking interface deprecations.
- Large (>2 reviewers, rollout needed): model-serving changes, KV cache layout, rollout-policy changes, public API changes. Break into canaries and explicit rollout plan.

Lightweight experiments to try (notes, follow up):
1) PR header template enforced by local git hook (pre-fill: TL;DR, scope, key-files, rollback). Quick A/B test with 5 engineers for two weeks.
2) "Review energy" tag in PR to indicate expected review time: tiny (<15m), small (15–30m), medium (30–60m), deep (>60m). See if reviewers respect it.
3) Add an automated checklist that runs on PR creation and fails CI if checklist items missing (but only for medium/deep).
4) Sample diff annotation bot: highlight lines that change control flow or auth checks (heuristic: changes in files under routing/ or auth/ or contains tokens like "authorize/permit/check").

Risk mitigations and micro-rollback patterns:
- Prefer additive changes + opt-in flags for behavior alterations.
- Always include a single revertable commit at the end with a one-line revert strategy in PR description.
- For migrations, include a compatibility shim and a two-phase rollout note.
- For perf-sensitive changes: include simple benchmark script + sample results in PR so reviewer can validate locally.

Followups / action items (me):
- Draft a one-page "PR posture" cheat sheet for the team (aim for 1 page, PDF). Due: 2025-11-21.
- Prototype the PR header template as a git commit-msg hook. Ask infra for opinion on automation by 11/28.
- Run A/B with 6 engineers on energy-tagging for 3 weeks, capture review times.
- Create a tiny GH action to inject a checklist UI into new PRs. Try to keep it opt-in.

Open questions / hypotheses to test:
- Will enforcing a stricter template increase review latency initially but reduce overall time-to-merge? Hypothesis: small initial cost, net win after 2 weeks.
- Are reviewers more likely to skip deep diffs if author states expected time? Might improve fairness of reviewer assignment.
- Can we automatically surface the minimal set of files a reviewer should read (heuristic/graph-based)? Worth a prototype.

Useful quick links and context references:
- PR that inspired this: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/892
- SRE notes on rollback strategies: JIRA ENG-1743
- Slack pilot thread: #eng-review (pinned messages)

Tiny template (copyable):
- TL;DR: <one sentence>
- Scope: <in scope / out of scope bullets>
- Key files: <file1, file2, file3>
- Rollback plan: <one-liner>
- Tests: <what was added / flakiness notes>
- Expected review time: <tiny/small/medium/deep>

Random thought: make a small rubric for reviewers to do a 10-minute scan: 1) read TL;DR + key files list, 2) open tests in parallel, 3) check for any auth/routing/persistence touched, 4) eyeball perf lines. If any red flag, escalate to a slow review (assign a second reviewer).

End notes: keep iterating. This doc will be a living lab draft — copy into a shared drive note once we have a couple experiments with data.
